name: Papua New Guinea Arokara AA, Eastern Highlands
origin: Papua New Guinea, Eastern Highlands (Arokara Cooperative, incl. Tairora and Gadsup)
vendor_notes: Dark chocolate, ripe plum and earthy tones; creamy body and wine-like acidity. Aroma 7/7, balance 7/7, brightness 5/7, body 5/7, sweetness 3/7. Grown 1,300-1,600 m.
goal: Light roast for espresso: plum and wine-like acidity over dark chocolate
rationale: Same Arokara cooperative and varieties as the Mile High A, which cracked at 187.3 C at 7:18 on this roaster, so FC is planned at 187 C. AA beans are larger, so the charge is a little gentler (188 C) to heat them through evenly without tipping. The long 36-hour fermentation gives the plum and wine notes that a light roast keeps. Sweetness is rated low (3/7), so for espresso development is a touch longer than the Mile High: ~10.5 C after first crack, DTR ~19%. If shots are sour, add 10-15 s of development.
steps: Preheat to 188 C, then hold steady 10+ min (BT/ET flat).
Charge 170 g at BT 188. Burner 72%, air 30, drum 90.
TP ~0:38 near 113 C. RoR is highest here, then falls.
At 177 C (~6:10): burner 46%. RoR ~10 and falling.
FC ~7:20 at ~187 C: burner 41%, air 50. Then 36%.
Drop ~9:05 at ~197.5 C (10.5 C after FC).

rest.note: Light washed PNG: give it at least 8 days. The plum, wine and dark chocolate come together around day 12.

history.note: Initial light-roast espresso plan from the Coffee Bean Corral page, calibrated to the measured opening on this roaster and the Mile High A roast (same cooperative): FC 187.3 C at 7:18.
